title: Fab City Dataset Entry
description: Canonical schema for a single dataset entry in the awesome-fabcity-data list. Each entry lives at data/{pillar}/{scale}/{slug}.yaml and is validated against this schema in CI.

name.description: Human-readable canonical name for the dataset / source.

url.description: Primary URL — landing page or registry entry.

description.description: One- to two-sentence summary. What is it; what does it carry; who runs it.

pillar.description: Which Full Stack Metrics Framework pillar this source primarily feeds.

scale.description: The scale tier where the source publishes its strongest signal. Some sources span scales; pick the one where the resolution is highest.

status.description: Operational status. live = current public read; stale = older than 12 months without update; paywalled = requires payment for full access; deprecated = officially retired; planned = upstream announced but not yet shipped.

license.description: License of the data itself, not the codebase. Use SPDX where possible (CC-BY-4.0, ODbL-1.0, CC0-1.0, MIT). Free-text OK if the source is multi-license.

api.description: Direct programmatic endpoint, if one exists. Null if download-only.

pilot_relevance.description: Which PLANETAI pilots (or 'global') this source has meaningful coverage for. Empty array means relevant elsewhere but not in current pilots.

tags.description: Free-form lowercase-hyphenated tags. Examples: air-quality, citizen-science, open-hardware, material-flow, procurement.

added.description: ISO date the entry was added to this list.

updated.description: ISO date of the last review of this entry's status / metadata.

wired_in_planetai.description: DEPRECATED, derived — read `adapter` instead. A hand-set boolean in this repository asserting runtime state in another one, which is why it drifted. The validator warns when this is true and `adapter` is absent. Kept only until the Airtable Data Sources mirror reads `adapter`; removed in the release after that.

adapter.description: What in planetai-node reads this source. `core:<fn>` names a function in app/sources.py or app/bootstrap.py (core:openmeteo_air, core:ckan, core:power_climatology); `pack:<id>` names a pack directory (pack:coast, pack:earth). Absent means no adapter exists — the source is registered and unread. Single-valued on purpose: when more than one reader exists, name the primary one here and the rest in notes.

feeds_cells.description: The Index cells a node fills from this source, in the node's own key spelling (Pillar|Scale, capitalised). Not the same as this entry's own pillar/scale, which say where the source publishes its strongest signal; feeds_cells says what a node does with it.

auth.description: What a node must hold to read this source. none = open call, no identification; key-free-rate-limited = open but throttled by IP; api-key = a key, issued without review; registration = an account or a signed agreement first; paid = money. Absent means unread from the entry's own licence/notes text, not none.

role.description: Whether this source tells a node what is happening (observe) or tells a person where to go and do something (act). Some sources are both. Absent means [observe] — the validator does not fill it in, consumers treat absence as observe.

act_kind.description: What kind of place or thing to act with. Required when role contains act, forbidden otherwise. build_readme.py renders a 🛠 badge from it. `equipment` is reserved for an OKW record of one facility's machines as an entry in its own right, and is not the right kind for a directory of facilities — that is `facility`.

upstream_listed_in.description: Other awesome-style lists or registries that already index this source. Helps avoid duplication of curation labour.

notes.description: Longer-form notes: API quirks, rate limits, licensing edge cases, recommended usage patterns, citation requirements.
